title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: simplest case: 1-equality / non-negative orthant LP. minx∈ℝ3c⊤xs.t.𝟏⊤x=1,x≥0. \min_{x \\mathbb{R}^3} \; c^\top x \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \mathbf{1}^\top x = 1, \; x \ge 0. SCS-style standard form Ax+s=bAx + s = b, s∈K={0}×ℝ+3s \K = \{0\} \times \mathbb{R}^3_+: Solve: expected optimum x=(1,0,0)x = (1, 0, 0) (cheapest non-zero coordinate). Now apply derivative small perturbation cc: agree finite-differencing perturbed solve:
code: A <- sparseMatrix(i = c(1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4),                   j = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3),                   x = c(1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1),                   dims = c(4, 3)) b <- c(1, 0, 0, 0) c <- c(1, 2, 3) cone_dict <- list(z = 1L, l = 3L) res <- solve_and_derivative(A, b, c, cone_dict, mode = "lsqr",                             tol_gap_abs = 1e-10,                             tol_gap_rel = 1e-10,                             tol_feas    = 1e-10) res$x #> [1] 1.000000e+00 1.562233e-11 5.329854e-12 dA <- sparseMatrix(i = integer(0), j = integer(0), x = numeric(0),                    dims = c(4, 3)) db <- numeric(4) dc <- c(0.001, 0, 0) d <- res$D(dA, db, dc) d$dx #> [1] -2.274114e-16 -6.059404e-16  4.396755e-15 res_pert <- solve_only(A, b, c + dc, cone_dict,                        tol_gap_abs = 1e-10,                        tol_gap_rel = 1e-10,                        tol_feas    = 1e-10) max(abs(d$dx - (res_pert$x - res$x))) #> [1] 1.453855e-14

title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: Minimum-distance---simplex inside Lorentz cone: mint,xts.t.∥x∥2≤t,𝟏⊤x=1. \min_{t, x} \; t \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \|x\|_2 \le t, \; \mathbf{1}^\top x = 1. Variables: (t,x1,x2,x3)(t, x_1, x_2, x_3). Standard form Ax+s=bAx + s = b one zero cone (equality) one SOC size 4 (containing (t,x)(t, x) block): optimum x=(1/3,1/3,1/3)x = (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) t=3/3≈0.577t = \sqrt{3}/3 \approx 0.577, achieving SOC equality constraint ∥x∥2=t\|x\|_2 = t.

title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: Minimum-eigenvalue 5×5 PSD matrix subject unit trace. Since PSD vectorisation SCS / diffcp follows lower-triangular column-major order sqrt(2) scaling -diagonals, build trace-coefficient row hand: optimal XX trace 1 concentrates eigenvector CC -negative eigenvalue, X≈e5e5⊤X \approx e_5 e_5^\top.
code: DIM <- 5L n   <- DIM * (DIM + 1L) %/% 2L          # 15  trace_row <- numeric(n) pos <- 1L for (col in seq_len(DIM)) {   trace_row[pos] <- 1.0   pos <- pos + (DIM - col + 1L)         # advance to next diagonal entry }  A <- rbind(   Matrix(matrix(trace_row, nrow = 1L), sparse = TRUE),   -Diagonal(n)) A <- as(A, "CsparseMatrix") b <- c(1.0, numeric(n))  C <- matrix(0, DIM, DIM) C[1, 1] <- 1; C[DIM, DIM] <- -1 c_vec <- vec_symm(C)  cone_dict <- list(z = 1L, s = DIM)  res <- solve_only(A, b, c_vec, cone_dict,                   tol_gap_abs = 1e-10,                   tol_gap_rel = 1e-10,                   tol_feas    = 1e-10) X <- unvec_symm(res$x, DIM) sum(diag(X)) #> [1] 1 range(eigen(X, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values) #> [1] -2.080584e-12  1.000000e+00

title: Differentiating Through a Cone Program with diffcp
text: solve_and_derivative accepts two modes: mode = "lsqr" (default): matrix-free conjugate-gradient style iterative solve M operator. Memory-efficient appropriate large sparse problems. mode = "dense": build M dense matrix factor Eigen’s LDLT. Lower per-call cost problem small derivative applied many times different perturbations. modes produce numeric answer within solver tolerance; dense path matches Python’s (M^\top M).\text{ldlt}().\text{solve}(M^\top \cdot \text{rhs}) bit bit, LSQR path agrees dense path roughly 1e-6 (LSQR’s default atol = btol = 1e-8).

title: diffcp - Differentiating Through Cone Programs in R
text: diffcp R port Python diffcp package. computes derivative optimal solution convex cone program respect problem data, treating program implicit function. derivative exposed forward operator D(dA, db, dc) adjoint DT(dx, dy, ds), can evaluated either dense (Eigen LDLT) matrix-free (LSQR) mode. implementation faithful port C++ core (cones, LinearOperator, dprojection, M operator, LSQR) cvxgrp/diffcp, called R via RcppEigen. R-level API mirrors Python source. Test fixtures pinned Python diffcp’s outputs two packages agree bit--bit every supported cone type.

title: diffcp - Differentiating Through Cone Programs in R
text: Given problem data (, b, c) (optionally quadratic objective P), diffcp solves primal–dual pair K Cartesian product standard cones (zero, non-negative orthant, second-order, positive semidefinite, exponential, exponential dual). returns optimal (x, y, s) together two callables: D(dA, db, dc) — applies derivative (x, y, s) respect (, b, c) perturbations (dA, db, dc). DT(dx, dy, ds) — applies adjoint, returning perturbations (dA, db, dc) corresponding desired change (dx, dy, ds) solution.
code: minimise    c'x          minimise    b'y subject to  Ax + s = b   subject to  A'y + c = 0             s in K                   y in K*

title: diffcp - Differentiating Through Cone Programs in R
text: larger examples — including PSD exponential cones — see package vignette (vignette("diffcp", package = "diffcp")).
code: library(diffcp)  ## Tiny LP: minimise c'x s.t. 1'x = 1, x >= 0  with n = 3 A <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(   i = c(1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4),   j = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3),   x = c(1, -1, 1, -1, 1, -1),   dims = c(4, 3)) b <- c(1, 0, 0, 0) c <- c(1, 2, 3) cone_dict <- list(z = 1L, l = 3L)  res <- solve_and_derivative(A, b, c, cone_dict, mode = "lsqr") res$x   # primal optimum res$y   # dual variable res$s   # slack  ## Apply the derivative at a perturbation in c. dA <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = integer(0), j = integer(0),                             x = numeric(0), dims = c(4, 3)) db <- numeric(4) dc <- c(0.001, 0, 0) res$D(dA, db, dc)   # list(dx, dy, ds)  ## Apply the adjoint to dx = c (steepest descent of c'x in (A, b, c)). res$DT(c, numeric(4), numeric(4))   # list(dA, db, dc)

title: diffcp - Differentiating Through Cone Programs in R
text: PSD vectorisation follows SCS convention (lower-triangular column-major, -diagonals scaled sqrt(2)). solving PSD problems Clarabel, diffcp automatically permutes rows entries b SCS order Clarabel’s upper-triangular order, permutes dual y slack s back return. Quadratic objectives (P) supported solve_only(P = P) forward solve via Clarabel SCS native QP. dense LSQR modes solve_and_derivative support quadratic objectives; upstream Python package handles QP via lpgd modes, R port yet provide.

title: diffcp 0.1.0
text: solve_only(, b, c, cone_dict, ...) — forward solve convex cone program via Clarabel (default) SCS, supporting six standard cones (zero, nonneg, SOC, PSD, exponential, exponential dual). Quadratic objectives via P argument supported forward-mode (mirroring Python diffcp). solve_and_derivative(, b, c, cone_dict, mode, ...) — solves cone program returns optimal (x, y, s) together two callables D(dA, db, dc) DT(dx, dy, ds) apply derivative adjoint supplied perturbations. mode = "lsqr" (default): matrix-free LSQR via M operator. mode = "dense": dense M matrix factored Eigen LDLT. pi(x, cones, dual) — projection onto Cartesian product cones, dual = TRUE selecting dual product cone. PSD-cone forward solves Clarabel automatically permute rows entries b SCS lower-triangular ordering Clarabel upper-triangular ordering, permute y / s back return.
